title: May the divine Waters be a blessing

words.meaning: for help, for what is wished
words.context: Bhāskara: «अभीष्टफलसिद्धये», for the attainment of what is wished
Bhāskara: the calming of what has come, «आगतानां रोगभयादीनां शमनम्»
Bhāskara: keeping off what has not yet come

sandhi.rule: -m before n is the class nasal; -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o

morphology.note: the old nominative plural in -īḥ (later देव्यः); Bhāskara notes the long vowel.
an old indeclinable, almost always paired with śam: ‘welfare and health’.

translation.literal: For welfare to us, the divine Waters, for help — may they be for drinking; welfare and health may they flow towards us.
translation.readable: May the divine Waters be a blessing to us, for help and for drinking; may they flow to us with welfare and health.

meaning: A prayer to the Waters as goddesses (RV 10.9.4, in the hymn whose first three verses are āpo hi ṣṭhā; TB 1.2.1). May they be a blessing to us, for help and for drinking, and may they flow towards us with śaṃ and yoḥ. Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara explains the two old words: śam is the calming of ills that have come, yoḥ the keeping off of those that have not. In the Brāhmaṇa it belongs to the installing of the sacred fires: the ground is sprinkled with water. The verse addresses the Waters; its first words, śaṃ no, sound like the graha’s name, Śani.
in_the_rite: The mantra of Śanaiścara (Saturn), first of the three in his step of the Navagraha sūktam (witness S). The verse itself addresses the Waters; what links it to Śani is the sound of its opening, śaṃ no. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara gives its use in the Brāhmaṇa’s rite of installing the fires: «अद्भिरवोक्षति - शंनो देवीरिति गायत्र्या» — he sprinkles with water, with this gāyatrī.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara: the Waters are to be a blessing «अभीष्टफलसिद्धये», for the attaining of what is wished, and «पीतये पानाय च भवन्तु», for drinking; śam is «आगतानां रोगभयादीनां शमनम्», the calming of illness and fear that have come, and yoḥ keeps away those that have not.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A gāyatrī of three pādas of eight syllables, printed as three lines.

notes.label: historical
notes.text: In the Ṛgveda (10.9.4) the verse follows āpo hi ṣṭhā, the three ṛks to the Waters recited in the Sandhyāvandanam.
